correctness.rationale: For any strictly improving cross-part relocation, the fractional utility inequality is d/b>(c-1)/(a-1) when b>0, and factorial potential ratio is ((a-1)d)/((c-1)b) (or times Q if c=1). For b=0 and source mixed the ratio (a-1)/(c-1) (or Q(a-1)) is >1; source occupancy one and same-part jumps cannot improve. Finite state space ensures termination for any finite types and allowed vacancies. With two types, a mixed source opposing a vacancy contradicts the sum of its two no-improvement inequalities; all stable assignments partition into globally pure, one-part-vacant with opposite full part pure, or both parts partly vacant with opposite pure occupied parts. Labeled vacancy counts give the displayed polynomial; fixed q balanced asymptotics follow from dominant 2 binom(m,q)2^{m-q+1} term. Independent exact rational enumeration checked 16,901 states, 34,776 improving jumps and 36 polynomials across bounded graphs; this is corroboration, not the all-parameter proof.
